summary.headline: GTPL Hathway Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 12% YoY to INR 1,020 crore, but net profit fell to INR 2.3 crore on higher depreciation and finance cost.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 12% YoY and 9% QoQ to INR 1,020 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR 109 crore (10.7% margin) and net profit of INR 2.3 crore. Management attributed the PAT decline of about INR 8 crore YoY mainly to a roughly INR 6 crore rise in depreciation and finance cost from capitalising right-of-use assets for HITS infrastructure. Standalone total revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 693 crore, with standalone EBITDA of INR 64.4 crore (9.3%) and net profit of INR 1.9 crore. The company signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital TV business of 7 ACT Group companies for INR 36.23 crore cash, with about 6 lakh subscribers, targeted to close by 15 September 2026.

segments.name: Digital TV
segments.commentary: Subscriber base of 9.60 million at 30 June 2026, of which 8.9 million paying; business partners above 51,000. Management said Digital TV revenue declined YoY as new, lower-ARPU markets dilute the mix; the Digital TV capex is about 50% of the INR 400 crore FY27 plan.

segments.name: Broadband
segments.commentary: Active subscribers of 1.06 million, up 10,000 YoY; ARPU INR 470; average data consumption 436 GB per user per month, up 6% YoY. Home pass base 5.95 million with about 75% FTTX-ready; extraction rate about 16-17%.

guidance_outlook: ACT acquisition (INR 36.23 crore, about 6 lakh digital TV subscribers across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Karnataka) to close by 15 September 2026; contribution expected from Q2 mid-quarter and fuller effect in Q3; no revenue or EBITDA contribution figures given yet.
Operating margin (22% currently) expected to rise to about 25% as HITS benefits materialise.
HITS savings expected to reach about 40-50% of benefit in FY27 and 100% from FY28; management expects full benefits from end-Q3 to start-Q4 FY27.
FY27 capex planned at about INR 400 crore, split roughly 50% broadband and 50% digital TV.
Broadband ARPU expected to stay around INR 470 in the near term; broadband extraction targeted at 19-20% (later 20-21%) on the existing home pass base.
Broadband launch planned in Kerala and Jammu & Kashmir soon; new markets expected to take 6-12 months to turn cash-positive.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at about INR 400 crore, roughly 50% broadband and 50% digital TV.
Home pass base of 5.95 million with about 75% FTTX-ready; management said it is not adding home passes for now but plans to invest in more home passes later.
HITS platform: about 2.5 million existing subscribers migrated and about 200,000 new subscribers added; total on platform close to 2.7 million since launch in February-March 2026.
HITS saved about INR 4 crore of bandwidth cost in Q1 FY27.

Entered Kerala and Jammu & Kashmir in Q1 FY27 via HITS (Digital TV first); addressable TV households about 6.5-7 million in Kerala and 4.5-5 million in J&K; existing base about 75,000-80,000 in Kerala.
Company said it has entered 26 states and 5 UTs, with only 2 states and 3 UTs left to cover.
demand_pricing: Broadband ARPU rose to INR 470 from INR 465, driven by subscribers moving from lower to higher-speed packages; management said ARPU was INR 400-420 two to three years ago.
Digital TV revenue fell YoY although active and paying subscribers were stable; management attributed this to churn and entry into lower-ARPU new markets.
Combo product (cable plus broadband plus OTT/games) is being upsold to both cable and broadband subscribers; pilot in some cities.
Content cost increases handled through negotiation with broadcasters, with partial absorption by the company and price increases in the market.
Entering new markets requires discounts; management said cable markets take 6-12 months to become profitable.
Management cited a large headroom: about 210 million TV households out of 350 million, and about 50 million FTTX broadband homes out of 3 billion households.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall sharply despite 12% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT fell about INR 8 crore YoY, mainly from a roughly INR 6 crore rise in depreciation and finance cost from capitalising HITS right-of-use assets; EBITDA was only about INR 3 crore lower, and HITS savings are yet to flow through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACT acquisition's expected contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give revenue or EBITDA figures before closing by 15 September 2026, and said the impact would appear from Q2 and more fully in Q3, with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana leadership (over 1 million existing subs there, rising to about 1.6-1.7 million).

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned FY27 capex and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 400 crore for FY27, split roughly 50% broadband and 50% digital TV.

qa_highlights.question: How will broadband conversion from the existing footprint improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Extraction is about 16-17% today, with a target of 19-21% on the 5.95 million home pass base; management also plans to invest in new home passes and recruited a new broadband CEO, Vivek Raina.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics and breakeven timing for the new Kerala and J&K markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no immediate breakeven, with a 6-12 month gestation period; STB costs scale per subscriber while fixed costs are low for digital TV, and broadband will need fixed-cost investment later.

qa_highlights.question: How does HITS change the cost structure versus traditional CATV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HITS costs are largely fixed, so margins rise with subscribers; it gave an example where point-to-point fibre delivery costs about INR 80 per subscriber per month in a town of 1,000 subscribers versus ARPU of about INR 125-130.

risks_watch: PAT margin is thin (INR 2.3 crore on INR 1,020 crore income) and depends on the HITS benefits arriving in Q3-Q4 FY27 as guided.
Digital TV revenue declined YoY; churn and lower-ARPU new markets could continue to weigh on the mix.
ACT deal closure by 15 September 2026 and integration; no financial guidance for the acquisition yet.
Broadband net adds are modest (10,000 YoY on 1.06 million); management has not yet shown a conversion ramp.
Content cost inflation and the need to absorb part of broadcaster cost increases.
Management did not disclose a source for the 25% operating margin target or the 19-21% extraction target; treat as aspirational.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and forward-looking on HITS, the ACT acquisition and the margin path, but was evasive on acquisition financials, declining to give revenue or EBITDA contribution until closing. Answers on PAT decline and Digital TV revenue decline leaned on future benefits rather than quantified drivers.
key_quotes: And that is because of the capitalization of right -of-use assets related to HITS infrastructure in line with the accounting standards and conservative accounting practice.
Right now, we don't want to give it. First, we let the integration happens and get the deal get closed as this is getting closed by 15th September as we announced in public.
So this year, you will see that somewhere around 40% to 50% benefit has come over the year because we are expanding doing the things. And from the next financial year, it will be 100%.
